einstellungen.text: Your wall is perfect. And nobody can get past it.
Setup day. You spent three nights building this display wall.
It stands right in the middle of the studio. Huge. White. Full of cards. You're proud of every single screw.
Your palm still has a mark from the screwdriver. It smells like fresh paint.
Eda tests the path. Her backpack gets stuck between the panels. The wood creaks.
"A wheelchair won't fit. Or a stroller."
Going around is forty meters. Past two stations nobody will see.
In your head, only one thing counts: three nights. Taking it down feels like losing.
In nineteen eighty-five, researchers found that time already spent can make people stick with a bad choice.
Those nights are gone. No matter what you do now. The only question is: what helps from tomorrow on?
You grab the screwdriver. The first screw squeaks.
An hour later, the middle is open. Light falls through the gap.
Eda walks through once. With her backpack. Without getting stuck.
You set the first piece in the corner. Yesterday you still called it your best work.
